newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 21.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* HOLLYWOOD - Time Warner's Warner Bros and MGM Inc have Hollywood's first home video licensing deal in China. The first Warner Home Video and MGM Home Video titles will be released in the Chinese market early next month. Warner and MGM have appointed Chinese government-owned conglomerate Shenzhen Advanced Science Enterprise Group as their licensee.

* HOLLYWOOD - Madonna has signed a deal to portray the photographer and revolutionary Tina Modotti, for Mick Jagger's Jagged Films. Jagger and Victoria Pearman will produced the film, based on a Modotti biography by Margaret Hooks and a screenplay by Michael Love and Martin Salinas.

* NEW YORK - Joel Schumacher has agreed to prepare for his third "Batman" sequel just two weeks after wrapping "Batman and Robin." Schumacher confirmed screenwriter Mark Protosevich has been hired to script the fifth installment in the franchise.
* HOLLYWOOD - Kevin Williamson, who wrote Dimension Films' horror film "Scream," has a seven-figure deal to write two sequels to the film for Walt Disney's Miramax Films.

* NEW YORK - Viacom's Paramount Pictures has acquired domestic distribution rights to first-time helmer Tony Vitale's "Kiss Me Guido" for about $2 million, according to sources. "Guido," which premiered last month at the Sundance Film Festival, is a comedy about a Bronx pizza maker who moves to Manhattan and unwittingly ends up with a gay roommate. It stars Nick Scotti, Anthony Barrile, Anthony DeSando and Craig Chester.
